b: Uma stood praying before Mother Mary. She didn't know how long she had stood there like that. Only when Rasamma from the next bed tapped her did she come back to herself.
"Don't pray to them, girl. Then you'll only get a girl! Pray to Kannan over there opposite. He'll be born to you himself, all plump and chubby..," said Rasamma.
Uma came back smiling and sat on the bed. If I pray to this Kannan and the baby is born dark, all the saffron milk I drank will go to waste, she thought, and laughed to herself.
Four o'clock. Looking at the clock, she rolled her eyes this way and that. Her eyes showed her longing for her husband, who still hadn't come though visiting time had begun.
"Fine. Let him come. It's only a few more days ... today or tomorrow. You'll see, his own son will come out and ask, Appa, don't you know how to come on time.." Uma said, a little too loudly.
Rasamma, who had just begun to doze, glared at Uma at the noise. Frightened, Uma turned her face towards the window opposite.

Outside, the rain was pouring down. In the whirling wind that blew with the rain, the windows banged and rattled. Uma didn't want to shut the window. Wasn't Uma the one who once roamed about like an untamed horse, just like that wind? And one man came along to tame even her!
Uma's heart swam in waves of memory. Siva! Him. She remembered Geetha teasing her: "Oh dear, you're supposed to call him Athaan, my friend."

"Siva! Siva! Siva! Saying his name does all sorts of things to me. If I told him this, he'd recite a poem about that too. Isn't he the one who won me over by reciting poems? Calling me an untamed horse, he recited a Bharathiyar poem to me for the very first time. What was it? .. Ah.
'O wind that comes
making the coconut fronds rustle,
we have made ourselves a heart
that rides you like a horse and roams'

So I'm the horse. Apparently I'm the one who has to carry him off. Oh my…...what thieves these boys are. When did I ever carry him off? He's the one who dragged me, every time he asked for a moment...."
How true it is that once love and desire take hold of a young woman's heart, they don't fade even when time passes!

"Even with a husband I loved and a happy family, there was a black spot, the witness to the life we lived. Ten years without a child, and the suffering I went through can't be told. And the sorrow Siva went through, more than me. Poor thing. He's the one who's mad about children. Even being called barren was all right. But when they spoke badly about Siva, that's when my heart broke. He stood there with tears in his eyes when he thought I couldn't see. But he'd never show me even a share of his sorrow. That's how much love."
"It's what childless people have always said: there's no treatment we didn't try. No temple we didn't go to. Only now has everything come together, that's God's will"
"Well, a hero is coming to take away all his troubles!"
A hand touched her shoulder, and Uma came back from the world of memory to the waking world. Siva stood in front of her, smiling.
"Is this your punctuality?" Uma asked, glaring.
"Sorry, di. A bit of work at the office.."
"How nice. The doctor has said the pains could come today or tomorrow. You stay at the office. When the baby's born I'll sign the papers myself and come home. Come straight home and see"
Siva laughed. "Just say the word. I'll resign and come and stay with you"
"Silly. Would you do something mad like that the moment I said it? Then who'll buy our boy his clothes? Who'll buy his powder?"
"So you've decided it's a boy?"
"Yes, da. It's definitely a boy. I know. Come and sit here next to me!"
Siva came and sat beside her.
"What name shall we give our boy?"
"Why are you in such a hurry now!"
"No. We have to think now. We should have thought ages ago. This is already late!!!"
"All right. I'm Siva. You're Uma. Let's call our boy Murugan"
"And I went and asked you. You're a proper old almanac. Forget you, I'll think of a nice name myself"
Siva laughed again. It seemed that smile would never leave his face, whatever happened.
"All right, whom should we invite to the naming ceremony? You tell me that too, Uma"
"Invite anyone you like, but never ever invite Radha next door!"
"Why, di? She's the one who gave you all that temple prasadam so you'd have a baby?"
"Never mind all that. She's the one who told the whole village it was your fault we couldn't have a child. Do you know how angry I am with her???"
"You love me that much?" said Siva, his eyes welling up.
"Why wouldn't I!" Uma laughed back innocently.
Next to them Rasamma had fallen asleep and was snoring loudly. "Look at her, tomorrow her baby will snore just like her," Uma said, and burst out laughing.
Siva felt like gathering up all the pearls that fell from her laughter and stringing them into a garland.
"Which estate is the Maharaja planning to buy?"
"You". "When I look at you, I feel like saying something…..”
"What? Tell me!….” she said, like a child.
"My lips command my fingers never to touch any food your lips have touched"
"Why? Do your lips want it for themselves?"
"No. They don't want food someone has tasted. They want the one who tasted it," he said mischievously.
Cheeks red with shyness could dim even the sun in the sky. That's how shy she was.
"Look, your appa wants another baby already. Hurry, hurry.."
Time ran out as they laughed and enjoyed themselves, and Siva set off.

Looking up from below, he saw Uma at the window, waving to him. How much love there was in her face. Love is the illness. Love is the medicine. Love is in everything. Siva laughed. Siva cried. And it seemed to him that the board reading "Mental Health Home" was laughing at him too.
note: Athaan is the affectionate Tamil word a wife or betrothed girl may use for her husband or cousin; "di" and "da" are intimate forms of address. Saffron milk is traditionally given to pregnant women in the belief that it gives the baby a fair complexion. The poem Siva recites is by Subramania Bharathi. "Old almanac" is Tamil slang for someone old-fashioned.
